limitations: No runtime probe or complete source listing was supplied, so exploitability and impact in the deployed environment were not independently verified.
The evidence also mentions a possible output-encoding issue, but this assessment focuses on the directly evidenced SQL injection.
remediation: Replace string concatenation with a PreparedStatement using a parameter placeholder for param.
Validate input according to the expected password format, but do not rely on validation alone.
Use a least-privileged database account and avoid exposing database errors to users.
Add regression tests covering injection metacharacters and authentication bypass attempts.
candidate.verdict_rationale: Observation "benchmark-open-code-review:BenchmarkTest00025:0031" shows direct concatenation of the request-derived parameter into SQL. This matches the unsafe pattern described in "KB-001" and "KB-EX-001".
verification_steps: Review the complete servlet code to confirm the source of param and the executed database statement.
Test in an authorized non-production environment using a harmless SQL-injection test payload.
Confirm whether the database account has excessive privileges and whether query execution produces altered results.
